intro: Every voice moment and character sound the original game plays, row by row: what the build maps, whether it has been heard in a build, and the proof. The reference for when a sound plays is OpenMW 0.51 as written down in docs/COMBAT.md, docs/ANIMATION.md and docs/NPC_VOICE_TABLE.md, and the builder's fallback test (tests/test_greeting_lut.py); the OpenMW source itself is not available on the build machine, so no row cites it line by line. Tribunal and Bloodmoon voices are out of scope until the expansions' NPCs are in the built world (NPC-VOICE-TABLE-ADDONS-54).
measured: The v0.0.57 release image's voice table, read back: 2,673 NPCs (2,675 from v0.0.58 with the two Orcs), every one with a voiced line (hit and attack 2,673, hello 2,648, idle, intruder, thief and flee 2,654); 396 creatures, every one with a sound (1,321 moments of their own, 1,760 by the shared fallback); 599 of the 601 sound records mapped; one named voice file the game data does not have (vo/d/f/Hit_DF007.mp3).

rows.moment: The player's pain grunts and death line; the enemies' taunts
rows.mapped: the player's Hit line by his race and sex (id1/npc-voice-player.txt, tools/greeting_lut.py player_voices) when hurt (30 %) and when killed; the enemies' Attack lines on the fight start and new swings. An approximation: the original filters the Hit infos with the player himself as speaker (race and sex, and also his class, faction, rank and the infos' other conditions); the voice table bakes each NPC's filter into its audience at build time and carries no race or sex condition, so AmiWind borrows the lines of the faction-less NPC of that race and sex with the commonest Hit set. It differs where a Hit info is limited to a class, a faction the player joins, or a condition on the speaker that the borrowed NPC passes and the player would not (or the reverse)
rows.proof: tests/test_greeting_lut.py, tests/aga_glut_test.c (a Breton man speaks a Breton man's lines); not yet heard in a build
